name: Short serve
doubles: Start most doubles rallies. Keep it tight to the tape so they can't kill; set up your partner at the net.
steps: Backhand grip, racket head above the hand, shuttle held out in front.
Same set-up every time so flick and short look identical.
Brush up the feathers with a short finger push — don't swing the arm.
Land just over the tape, ideally on the T or wide short.
Recover: racket up, ready to take the net or cover the flick miss.
mistakes: Serving too high above the tape

name: Flick serve
doubles: Punish receivers who crowd the net or sit on the short serve. Use sparingly so it stays a surprise.
steps: Identical preparation to the short serve.
At the last moment, tighten the fingers and punch the shuttle flat-ish toward the rear tramlines.
Aim deep to the backhand corner when you can.
Follow in — be ready for a weak return.
cues: Late finger punch, not a big swing
mistakes: Different stance/racket position that tips the flick
Never mixing it in, so they sit deep
vt: Drive Serve - The Popular New Serve in Badminton

name: Serve receive / push
doubles: Your first attack. Push tight short serves into the body or mid-court; don't gift a lift.
steps: Racket up at head height, left foot forward, loose grip (RH).
Weight on the front foot, ready to push or turn on a flick.
Meet short serves high — soft push to the body or mid-court gap.
On a flick: push off the front foot, turn sideways, racket stays above the head.
cues: Push short; turn and clear/drive flicks
mistakes: Sitting too deep so short serves die
Chasing flicks with the racket still low
vt: How To Return The Serve In Badminton + 2 effective doubles returns!

name: Net shot (tight net)
doubles: Force the lift. Meet it high near the tape so they can't kill; set up your partner's smash.
steps: Split step, then heel-to-toe lunge with chest up.
Meet the shuttle high near the tape — don't let it drop.
Loose grip, finger push: catch and place. No follow-through.
Racket face slightly open; soft over the tape.
Push back through the front heel to base, racket up.
cues: Meet it high near the tape
Loose grip finger push — catch and place
Heel-to-toe lunge, chest up, no follow-through
mistakes: Swinging through and popping it up
Folding at the waist in the lunge
vt: How To Hit A Perfect Doubles Net Shot EVERY TIME

name: Net spin / tumble
doubles: Make the tight net even harder to lift cleanly. Use when you arrive early.
steps: Same early arrival and high contact as a dead net.
Brush across the feathers (in-to-out or out-to-in) with fingers.
Keep the swing short — spin comes from the brush, not power.
Recover immediately; expect a lift or a weak net.
cues: Same recovery as a dead net
mistakes: Big arm swipe that hits the net
Watching the spin instead of recovering
vt: The 3 Different Singles Net Shots You Need To Know

name: Net kill
doubles: Put away anything above the tape. Your go-to finish at the net.
steps: Racket up early as soon as you see a high net return.
Lunge in with space between body and shuttle.
Tap not swing — finger snap, stop the racket dead after contact.
Aim steep down, straight or cross.
Recover or stay ready for a block rebound.
mistakes: Swiping / long follow-through into the net
Standing too close and getting jammed
Waiting until the shuttle drops below the tape
vt: The 2 Types Of NET KILL To Always Win The Point

name: Lift (forehand & backhand)
doubles: Reset when you're under pressure. High for time; flatter when you want to rush their rear court.
steps: Get the racket under the shuttle early with a relaxed grip.
Use legs and a compact forearm brush — don't muscle with the shoulder.
High lift: steep arc to the rear tramlines. Flat lift: lower trajectory to rush.
Turn and recover to base immediately — never admire it.
cues: High for time, flat to rush
mistakes: Lifting from the net when a net shot was on
Standing and watching after the lift

name: Drive
doubles: Keep the rally flat and fast. Take it early in front of the body to jam them.
steps: Split step; take the shuttle in front of the body, not beside the hip.
Compact punch with forearm rotation — short backswing.
Keep it flat and low over the net.
Stay on the balls of the feet for the next drive or block.
cues: Hit it before it crosses your body
Stay ready for the next one
mistakes: Driving cross when straight was safer
vt: How To Perfect Your Backhand Drive

name: Push
doubles: Soft mid-court pressure into the body or mid-court gap — between a net shot and a drive.
steps: Meet the shuttle early with a firm but soft hand.
Guide it into the body or the gap between opponents.
Little follow-through; racket returns to ready.
Use off the serve receive and off soft mid-court returns.
cues: Into the body or the gap
mistakes: Pushing too hard (becomes a drive they attack)
vt: How To Dominate The Mid-Court In Doubles

name: Block (smash defence)
doubles: Your strength. Soft hands take pace off the smash and drop it tight to the net.
steps: Wide base, racket out in front, soft grip.
Don't swing — meet the smash and cushion.
Angle the face so the shuttle dies at the net.
Recover toward the net or mid as the quality of the block allows.
mistakes: Hard blocking that sits up mid-court
Racket too late / beside the body
Lifting when a block was on
vt: How To Defend In Mixed Doubles

name: Forehand clear
doubles: Buy time and push them deep. Must land in the rear tramlines — mid-court clears get smashed.
steps: Turn sideways early; get behind the shuttle.
Belt buckle to the net first — hips lead.
Contact high and slightly in front; hit up and through.
Scissor or chassé recover to base.
cues: Behind it, then up and through
vt: Overhead Badminton Shots: Perfect Your Clear, Smash, and Drop

name: Backhand clear
doubles: Escape from the deep backhand corner. Prefer round-the-head when you have time; use true backhand when you don't.
steps: Turn early, elbow up, racket head above the hand.
Get under and slightly behind; thumb drive through.
Hit high to the rear tramlines.
Recover hard — this often leaves you out of position.
mistakes: Contact too low / in front → net or mid-court
Round-the-head avoided when it was on
vt: How To Play A Backhand - Backhand Drop, Clear and Smash!

name: Drop (slow / fast / slice)
doubles: Bring them in after a clear. Same preparation as smash/clear so they can't read it.
steps: Same overhead set-up as a clear or smash.
Slow drop: soften at contact, place just over the tape.
Fast drop: more pace, lands nearer the service line.
Slice: brush the side of the feathers to kill pace and add drift.
Recover in — expect a lift or net reply.
mistakes: Different preparation that tips the drop
vt: 4 Types of Dropshots from Beginner to Pro

name: Smash
doubles: Primary attacking weapon. Steep and placed beats wild pace.
steps: Turn, get behind it, belt buckle to the net.
Jump if you can; contact high and in front.
Wrist/forearm snap; aim at body or mid-court gap.
Scissor kick: land on the left foot (RH), weight going forward — not two-footed falling back.
Follow in toward the net.
cues: Scissor, land on left, go forward
mistakes: Smashes into the tramline body that they block cross
vt: 3 Things Pro Badminton Players Do On Their Smash

name: Jump smash
doubles: Higher contact = steeper angle. Use when the lift is high enough that you have time.
steps: Read the high lift early; load the jump.
Full scissor: plant, jump, smash at the top.
Land on the left foot (RH) moving forward.
Be ready to kill the next weak return at the net.
cues: Jump only when you have time
vt: Learn The Jump Smash! Step-By-Step Badminton Tutorial

name: Round-the-head smash / clear
doubles: Cover the deep backhand corner with a forehand. Essential in doubles rear-court play.
steps: For fast flat lifts: Malaysian left-right-left chassé into a one-leg jump.
For high clears: cross step behind, then full scissor-kick jump.
Belt buckle turns toward the net; hit smash or clear with the same prep.
Land on the left foot and recover to base.
vt: Badminton around the head SMASH tutorial (w. scissors jump)

name: Backhand rear-corner shot
doubles: Last resort when you can't get round the head. Clear high or soft drop — avoid a flat mid-court gift.
steps: Turn early; don't run facing the back.
Elbow high, compact thumb action.
Prefer a high clear to the tramlines or a soft drop.
Only drive/smash if the shuttle is high enough.
Sprint recover — partner covers the net.
mistakes: Trying a power smash from too low
No call so partner also goes
vt: How To Play A Backhand - Backhand Drop, Clear and Smash!
